cards.description: 该论文提出 GraphBARC，用图网络学习节点与边因子以形成全图联合信念，并结合解析贝叶斯更新与带决策认证的多步主动采样，从而以更少测量获得更准确的无线电地图。其价值在于把空间相关性与多步路线评估纳入同一框架，并降低规划计算开销。
cards.originalTitle: Learning Graph Beliefs for Active Radio Mapping With Decision-Certified Multi-Step Sensing
cards.limitations: 论文结论基于作者选取的基线与实验设置，RMSE 与规划时间的改进幅度不宜外推为普遍性能保证。决策认证依赖所建残差界与间隙界的具体假设，其有效性边界需结合原文条件核对；摘要未给出跨场景泛化与真实部署验证信息。
cards.whyItMatters: 无线电地图对网络优化与自主平台具有基础作用，而密集测量代价高。若该方法在更广泛场景中成立，可在保持地图精度的同时减少采样与规划开销，为主动感知中的多步决策提供可认证的计算路径。
cards.summary: 论文针对密集测量成本过高的问题，提出图结构化主动无线电地图构建框架 GraphBARC。该方法用图网络从已采测量中学习相关的节点与边因子，形成支持解析观测更新的全图信念，并以非短视策略评估多步路线的联合贝叶斯风险下降。作者报告相对基线平均 RMSE 降低超过 16%，核心规划时间相比固定精度、无剪枝实现减少 56%。
cards.whyItMattersEn: Radio maps are foundational for network optimization and autonomous platforms, yet dense measurement is costly. If the approach holds in broader settings, it could reduce sampling and planning overhead while maintaining map accuracy, and it offers a certifiable computational path for multi-step decisions in active sensing.
cards.summaryEn: To address the high cost of dense measurements, the paper proposes GraphBARC, a graph-structured active radio map construction framework. A graph network learns correlated node and edge factors from acquired measurements to form a full-map belief that supports analytical observation updates, and a nonmyopic strategy evaluates joint Bayes risk reduction over multi-step routes. The authors report over 16% lower mean RMSE than evaluated baselines and 56% less core planning time than a fixed-accuracy, unpruned implementation.
cards.title: 图信念建模与决策认证的多步主动无线电地图构建
cards.titleEn: Graph Belief Modeling and Decision-Certified Multi-Step Sensing for Active Radio Mapping
keyPointsEn: A graph network learns correlated node and edge factors to form a joint full-map belief that supports analytical observation updates without retraining.
A nonmyopic multi-step sensing strategy evaluates map-wide Bayes risk reduction and accounts for information redundancy among planned measurements.

Candidate responses are reused, and residual-based bounds plus an error-aware continuation bound prune unpromising prefixes; only responses needed for unresolved comparisons are refined, with a computable decision-gap bound.
keyPoints: 用图网络学习节点与边的相关因子，形成全图联合信念，并支持无需重训练的解析观测更新。
采用非短视多步传感策略，评估整图贝叶斯风险下降并考虑规划测量间的信息冗余。
通过复用候选响应、残差界与误差感知的延续界剪枝，仅细化未解决比较所需的响应，并给出可计算的决策间隙界。
cards.limitationsEn: The conclusions are based on the authors' chosen baselines and experimental settings, and the reported RMSE and planning-time improvements should not be generalized as universal performance guarantees. Decision certification relies on specific assumptions behind the residual and gap bounds, whose validity limits need to be checked against the original text; the abstract does not provide information on cross-scenario generalization or real-world deployment validation.
cards.descriptionEn: The paper proposes GraphBARC, a graph-structured active radio map construction framework that learns node and edge factors to induce a joint full-map belief, combines it with analytical Bayesian updates and decision-certified multi-step sensing, and aims to achieve more accurate maps with fewer measurements. Its value lies in integrating spatial correlation and multi-step route evaluation within one framework while reducing planning computation.

cards.description: 该研究提出CausalVisionRI系统，将观测发现的因果图作为先验约束融入深度学习，用于西北太平洋热带气旋24小时快速增强预警。其新意在于以可审计的因果结构指导模型训练，并在2020-2024年前向留出集上显著优于四个参考系统，为物理知情预警提供新路径。
cards.originalTitle: Causal-prior-constrained deep learning for rapid-intensification warning of western North Pacific tropical cyclones
cards.limitations: 研究仅覆盖西北太平洋2000-2017年522个气旋的因果发现与2020-2024年3004条记录的前向验证；因果图通路的显著贡献仅在一个集合成员中成立，整体增益有限；未评估其他海盆或更长时期的泛化性，且预警标准基于USA 30-kt与RITCF，结论不宜直接外推为业务部署依据。
cards.whyItMatters: 快速增强是热带气旋中最危险且难以预测的阶段，该工作表明观测因果结构可约束深度学习，提升预警技能并提供物理可解释路径，对防灾减灾有潜在价值。
cards.summary: 研究构建了因果先验约束的深度学习系统CausalVisionRI，融合红外遥感、大气海洋场与观测因果图，实现西北太平洋24小时快速增强预警。在2020-2024年前向留出集的3004条记录上，五成员集合的Brier技能分（BSS）为0.259，显著超过四个参考系统（三个LDA基线最高0.105）。消融实验表明因果图通路在留出集上贡献0.032 BSS，在2020-2021年贡献0.063，且在一个集合成员中贡献显著。
cards.whyItMattersEn: Rapid intensification is among the most dangerous and unpredictable phases of tropical cyclones. This work shows that observational causal structure can constrain deep learning to improve warning skill and provide physically interpretable pathways, with potential value for disaster risk reduction.
cards.summaryEn: The study builds CausalVisionRI, a causal-prior-constrained deep-learning system that fuses infrared remote sensing, atmospheric and oceanic fields, and an observational causal graph for 24-h rapid-intensification warning in the western North Pacific. On a forward holdout of 3,004 records from 2020–2024, the five-member ensemble achieves a Brier skill score (BSS) of 0.259, significantly exceeding four reference systems (three LDA baselines reach at most 0.105). Ablations show the graph pathway adds 0.032 BSS across the holdout and 0.063 over 2020–2021, with a significant contribution in one ensemble member.
cards.title: 因果先验约束深度学习提升西北太平洋热带气旋快速增强预警
cards.titleEn: Causal-Prior-Constrained Deep Learning Improves Rapid-Intensification Warning for Western North Pacific Tropical Cyclones
keyPointsEn: CausalVisionRI integrates an observationally discovered causal graph and eight sign-verified effects as an auditable prior, unifying infrared imagery, atmospheric and oceanic fields, and the cyclone's dynamical and structural state.
On the forward holdout (2020–2024, 3,004 records), the five-member ensemble achieves a BSS of 0.259, significantly outperforming four reference systems (LDA baselines at most 0.105).
Ablations show the graph pathway adds 0.032 BSS across the holdout and 0.063 over 2020–2021, with a significant contribution in one ensemble member.
keyPoints: CausalVisionRI将观测发现的因果图与八个符号验证效应作为可审计先验，统一红外影像、大气海洋场和热带气旋动力结构状态。
在前向留出集（2020-2024年，3004条记录）上，五成员集合BSS达0.259，显著优于四个参考系统（LDA基线最高0.105）。
消融显示因果图通路在留出集增加0.032 BSS，在2020-2021年增加0.063，并在一个集合成员中贡献显著。
cards.limitationsEn: The study covers causal discovery from 522 cyclones in 2000–2017 and forward validation on 3,004 records from 2020–2024 only in the western North Pacific; the significant contribution of the graph pathway holds in only one ensemble member, and overall gains are modest; generalization to other basins or longer periods is not evaluated, and warning standards are based on USA 30-kt and RITCF, so conclusions should not be directly extrapolated as operational deployment evidence.
cards.descriptionEn: The study introduces CausalVisionRI, a deep-learning system that integrates an observationally discovered causal graph as a prior constraint for 24-h rapid-intensification warning of western North Pacific tropical cyclones. Its novelty lies in using auditable causal structure to guide training, and it significantly outperforms four reference systems on a 2020–2024 forward holdout, offering a new route to physically informed warning.

cards.description: 提出模块化离线贝叶斯分割框架BayesBreak，将局部块评分与全局动态规划推断分离，支持不规则观测、多序列共享边界及潜在组设计，并在共轭指数族下实现精确推断，非共轭情形可结合局部近似。
cards.originalTitle: Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Segmentation with Irregular Designs, Multi-Sequence Hierarchies, and Grouped/Latent-Group Designs
cards.limitations: 论文摘要仅报告了合成数据验证与四个真实数据示例，未提供与现有方法的全面比较或大规模性能评估；非共轭情形的推断依赖局部近似，其准确性未在摘要中量化；稳定性界仅针对均匀块证据误差，实际误差分布可能影响界紧性。
cards.whyItMatters: 该框架扩展了贝叶斯分割模型的适用性，使其能处理不规则设计、多序列层次和潜在组结构，同时保持不确定性量化与推断稳定性，为地质、基因组、金融等领域的变点分析提供通用工具。
cards.summary: BayesBreak是一个模块化离线贝叶斯分割框架，通过分离局部块评分与全局动态规划，实现对分割数、边界和潜在信号的后验推断。对于加权指数族似然与共轭先验，块证据和后验矩可由累积充分统计量闭式获得，从而精确计算后验、边界边际及贝叶斯回归曲线。框架还支持设计感知分区先验、重复序列精确池化及潜在模板混合的精确EM更新，并给出后验几率稳定性界。
cards.whyItMattersEn: The framework extends the applicability of Bayesian segmentation models to irregular designs, multi-sequence hierarchies, and latent group structures while maintaining uncertainty quantification and inference stability, offering a general tool for change-point analysis in geology, genomics, finance, and other fields.
cards.summaryEn: BayesBreak is a modular offline Bayesian segmentation framework that separates local block scoring from global dynamic programming to infer posteriors over segment counts, boundaries, and latent signals. For weighted exponential-family likelihoods with conjugate priors, block evidences and posterior moments are available in closed form from cumulative sufficient statistics, enabling exact sum-product inference and Bayes regression curves. The framework also supports design-aware partition priors, exact pooling across replicates with shared boundaries, and latent-template mixtures with exact EM updates, and provides a posterior-odds stability bound.
cards.title: 贝叶斯分割框架BayesBreak支持不规则设计与多序列层次
cards.titleEn: BayesBreak: A Bayesian Segmentation Framework for Irregular Designs and Multi-Sequence Hierarchies
keyPointsEn: Separates local block scoring from global dynamic programming, enabling exact sum-product inference and a separate max-sum MAP segmentation.

Under conjugate exponential families, block evidences and posterior moments have closed forms; non-conjugate GLM blocks can use local approximations such as Laplace, variational methods, EP, or quadrature.
Supports design-aware partition priors for irregular observations, exact pooling across replicates with shared boundaries, and latent-template mixtures with exact EM updates.
keyPoints: 分离局部块评分与全局动态规划，支持精确sum-product推断与独立max-sum MAP分割。
共轭指数族下块证据和后验矩有闭式解，非共轭GLM块可使用Laplace、变分、EP或求积等局部近似。
支持不规则观测的设计感知分区先验、多序列共享边界精确池化及潜在模板混合的精确EM更新。
cards.limitationsEn: The abstract reports only synthetic validation and four real-data illustrations, without comprehensive comparisons to existing methods or large-scale performance evaluation; inference in non-conjugate cases relies on local approximations whose accuracy is not quantified in the abstract; the stability bound addresses uniform per-block evidence errors, and actual error distributions may affect bound tightness.
cards.descriptionEn: BayesBreak is a modular offline Bayesian segmentation framework that separates local block scoring from global dynamic-programming inference, supporting irregular observations, shared boundaries across sequences, and latent-group designs with exact inference under conjugate exponential families and local approximations for non-conjugate cases.

cards.description: 该项目提出一种新路径：不依赖屏幕像素猜测，而是通过操作系统无障碍树读取任意应用的界面结构，使智能体能稳定识别元素并安全重试操作。
cards.limitations: 当前信息仅来自项目自述和 GitHub Trending 条目，缺乏独立评测、性能数据与安全性分析；无障碍树覆盖范围因应用和操作系统而异，实际可靠性尚未验证。
cards.whyItMatters: 若该思路可行，桌面智能体可减少对视觉识别的依赖，在更多应用上实现稳定操作，降低因界面变化导致的失败风险。
cards.summary: Agent Desktop 是 Vercel Labs 发布的开源项目，旨在让智能体在桌面上可靠地使用计算机。它用 Rust 构建，通过操作系统无障碍树获取任意应用的界面结构，使元素引用保持稳定，动作可安全重试，而非基于像素猜测。项目描述属于作者主张，尚未提供独立验证的性能或安全性数据。
cards.whyItMattersEn: If viable, this approach could reduce desktop agents' reliance on visual recognition, enabling stable operation across more apps and lowering failure risk from UI changes.
cards.summaryEn: Agent Desktop is an open-source project from Vercel Labs that aims to give agents reliable computer use on the desktop. Built in Rust, it obtains the UI structure of any app through OS accessibility trees, keeping element references stable and actions safe to retry rather than relying on pixel guessing. The project description reflects the authors' claims; no independent performance or safety data is provided.
cards.title: Agent Desktop：借助操作系统无障碍树让智能体可靠操作桌面应用
cards.titleEn: Agent Desktop: Reliable Desktop App Operation via OS Accessibility Trees
keyPointsEn: Reads any app's UI structure through OS accessibility trees instead of pixel-level guessing.
Keeps element references stable and actions safe to retry, improving desktop agent reliability.
Built with Rust and trending on GitHub Trending Daily.
keyPoints: 通过操作系统无障碍树读取任意应用的界面结构，替代像素级猜测。
元素引用保持稳定，操作可安全重试，提升桌面智能体可靠性。
项目使用 Rust 构建，在 GitHub Trending Daily 中受到关注。
cards.limitationsEn: Current information comes only from the project's self-description and a GitHub Trending entry, lacking independent evaluation, performance data, and security analysis. Accessibility tree coverage varies by app and OS, and actual reliability remains unverified.
cards.descriptionEn: The project proposes a new approach: instead of guessing from screen pixels, it reads any app's UI structure through OS accessibility trees, enabling agents to identify elements stably and retry actions safely.

cards.description: 提出OMSO方法，利用求解器执行结果作为廉价结果标签进行强化学习，无需过程级监督，并可在不同求解器环境间迁移，提升优化建模的推理与语义正确性。
cards.originalTitle: Learning to Model Optimization Problems from Solver Outcomes
cards.limitations: 证据基于arXiv预印本，尚未经同行评审；实验限于特定数据集与求解器组合，跨更多问题类型和求解器的泛化性需进一步验证；奖励信号仅来自执行结果，可能忽略建模过程中的语义错误；未评估实际部署中的推理延迟与成本。
cards.whyItMatters: 该方法为优化建模提供了一种低成本、可迁移的强化学习范式，减少对闭源LLM和过程监督的依赖，有望推动决策智能的可扩展自动化。
cards.summary: 现有LLM优化建模方法依赖闭源智能体管线（高延迟）或过程监督微调小模型（成本高且易过拟合单一求解器API）。作者提出OMSO，将数学规划求解器作为确定性交互环境，以生成-执行-反馈-更新的闭环强化学习，仅用执行结果作为标量奖励。在多个数据集和求解器上的实验显示，OMSO匹配或超越过程监督SFT，并支持零样本迁移和直接RL训练。
cards.whyItMattersEn: This method offers a low-cost, transferable reinforcement learning paradigm for optimization modeling, reducing reliance on closed-source LLMs and process supervision, and potentially advancing scalable automation of decision intelligence.
cards.summaryEn: Existing LLM-based optimization modeling approaches rely on closed-source agentic pipelines with high latency or process-supervised fine-tuning of smaller models that is costly and overfits to a single solver API. The authors propose OMSO, which treats a mathematical programming solver as a deterministic interactive environment and learns via a closed-loop generate-execute-feedback-update reinforcement learning process using only execution outcomes as scalar rewards. Experiments across multiple datasets and solvers show that OMSO matches or outperforms process-supervised SFT and supports zero-shot transfer and direct RL training.
cards.title: 基于求解器结果反馈的优化建模强化学习
cards.titleEn: Reinforcement Learning for Optimization Modeling from Solver Outcomes
keyPointsEn: OMSO uses solver execution outcomes as reward signals, eliminating process-level supervision and reducing annotation costs.
Cross-solver generalization is achieved by switching solver environments rather than reconstructing datasets for each solver.
On NL4OPT, MAMO, IndustryOR, and OptiBench across Gurobi, OR-Tools, and COPT, OMSO matches or outperforms process-supervised SFT.
keyPoints: OMSO以求解器执行结果为奖励信号，无需过程级监督，降低标注成本。
通过切换求解器环境实现跨求解器泛化，避免为每个求解器重建数据集。
在NL4OPT、MAMO、IndustryOR和OptiBench上，跨Gurobi、OR-Tools和COPT，OMSO匹配或超越过程监督SFT。
cards.limitationsEn: Evidence is based on an arXiv preprint not yet peer-reviewed; experiments are limited to specific dataset-solver combinations, and generalization to more problem types and solvers requires further validation; reward signals come only from execution outcomes and may overlook semantic errors in modeling; inference latency and cost in real deployment are not evaluated.
cards.descriptionEn: Proposes OMSO, which uses solver execution outcomes as cheap outcome labels for reinforcement learning, eliminating process-level supervision and enabling transfer across heterogeneous solver environments to improve modeling reasoning and semantic correctness.

cards.description: 针对多智能体辩论中有限上下文窗口与非结构化记忆难以恢复相关论据的问题，HEDGE 将辩论轨迹表示为语义超图，并引入学习式记忆选择模块（MSM）决定存储、备份或省略记忆候选。在七个基准上，HEDGE 平均准确率较最强多智能体基线（GPT-4o-mini）提升5.0分，冲突密集任务提升8.2分，同时减少48%记忆使用与34%辩论轮数。
cards.originalTitle: HEDGE: Gated Hypergraph Memory for Scalable Multi-Agent Debate
cards.limitations: 证据边界包括：结果仅基于论文所选七个基准和特定基线（最强多智能体系统为 GPT-4o-mini），未涵盖其他模型或开放域任务；5.0分、8.2分、48%和34%等数字均为论文报告值，尚未经独立复现；超图构建与 MSM 训练引入额外复杂度，其计算成本与跨领域泛化性未在摘要中说明；作者关于“选择性记忆更好捕捉高阶关系”的因果解释属于观点，需进一步实验验证。
cards.whyItMatters: 多智能体辩论的实际部署受限于上下文窗口和记忆冗余，HEDGE 提供了一种结构化记忆管理与选择性保留的框架。若其结果可复现，则表明超图表示与学习式记忆路由能在提升准确率的同时降低记忆开销和辩论轮数，对构建可扩展的多智能体推理系统具有参考价值。
cards.summary: 多智能体辩论系统需要跨轮次保留和回溯论点，但上下文窗口受限且记忆缺乏结构，使得相关信息难以有效恢复；现有扁平或成对图记忆难以刻画多智能体同意、证据冲突与共识演化等高阶关系。作者提出 HEDGE，用语义超图连接跨智能体的相关主张，并在超边内部保留细粒度论辩结构，再通过监督学习与强化学习训练的记忆选择模块将每个记忆候选路由至存储、备份或省略。在七个基准上，HEDGE 平均准确率较最强多智能体系统（GPT-4o-mini）提升5.0分，冲突密集任务提升8.2分，记忆使用减少48%，辩论轮数减少34%。上述性能数字为论文报告的实验结果，而“选择性记忆能更好捕捉高阶论辩关系”是作者的解释性观点，需独立验证。
cards.whyItMattersEn: Practical deployment of multi-agent debate is constrained by context windows and memory redundancy, and HEDGE offers a framework for structured memory management and selective retention. If its results are reproducible, they suggest that hypergraph representations and learned memory routing can improve accuracy while reducing memory overhead and debate rounds, providing a reference for building scalable multi-agent reasoning systems.
cards.summaryEn: Multi-agent debate systems need to retain and revisit arguments across rounds, but limited context windows and unstructured memories make relevant information hard to recover, and existing flat or pairwise-graph memories struggle to capture higher-order relations such as multi-agent agreement, conflicting evidence, and evolving consensus. The authors propose HEDGE, which connects related claims across agents via semantic hyperedges while preserving fine-grained argumentative structure within each hyperedge, and trains a memory selection module with supervised and reinforcement learning to route each memory candidate to STORE, BACKUP, or OMIT. On seven benchmarks, HEDGE improves average accuracy by 5.0 points over the strongest multi-agent system (GPT-4o-mini), gains 8.2 points on conflict-heavy tasks, reduces memory usage by 48%, and reduces debate rounds by 34%. These performance figures are reported experimental results, while the claim that selective memory better captures higher-order argumentative relations is the authors' explanatory view and requires independent validation.
cards.title: HEDGE：门控超图记忆用于可扩展多智能体辩论
cards.titleEn: HEDGE: Gated Hypergraph Memory for Scalable Multi-Agent Debate
keyPointsEn: HEDGE models debate trajectories as semantic hypergraphs: hyperedges connect related claims across agents, and intra-hyperedge relational graphs preserve fine-grained argumentative structure.
The memory selection module (MSM), trained with supervised learning and reinforcement learning, routes memory candidates to STORE, BACKUP, or OMIT to retain useful information and limit redundancy.

On seven benchmarks, HEDGE improves average accuracy by 5.0 points over the strongest multi-agent baseline, gains 8.2 points on conflict-heavy tasks, reduces memory usage by 48%, and reduces debate rounds by 34%.
keyPoints: HEDGE 将辩论轨迹建模为语义超图：超边连接跨智能体的相关主张，超边内关系图保留细粒度论辩结构。
记忆选择模块（MSM）经监督学习与强化学习训练，将记忆候选路由到 STORE、BACKUP 或 OMIT，以保留有用信息并抑制冗余。
在七个基准上，HEDGE 较最强多智能体基线平均准确率提升5.0分，冲突密集任务提升8.2分，记忆使用减少48%，辩论轮数减少34%。
cards.limitationsEn: Evidence boundaries include: results are based only on the seven benchmarks and specific baselines chosen in the paper (the strongest multi-agent system being GPT-4o-mini), without covering other models or open-domain tasks; figures such as 5.0 points, 8.2 points, 48%, and 34% are reported values not yet independently reproduced; hypergraph construction and MSM training add complexity, and their computational cost and cross-domain generalization are not described in the abstract; the authors' causal explanation that selective memory better captures higher-order relations is a viewpoint that requires further experimental validation.
cards.descriptionEn: To address limited context windows and unstructured memories that make relevant arguments hard to recover in multi-agent debate, HEDGE represents debate trajectories as semantic hypergraphs and introduces a learned memory selection module (MSM) that routes each memory candidate to STORE, BACKUP, or OMIT. Across seven benchmarks, HEDGE improves average accuracy by 5.0 points over the strongest multi-agent baseline (GPT-4o-mini), reaches 8.2 points on conflict-heavy tasks, and

cards.description: Scrapling 是一个网络抓取框架，宣称能处理从单次请求到全规模抓取的任务。其价值在于为不同规模的抓取需求提供统一工具，但具体能力需参考项目文档验证。
cards.limitations: 输入信息仅为 GitHub Trending 的项目简介，缺少技术文档、基准测试或用户反馈。无法确认其是否真正优于现有框架，也不清楚其具体功能边界、性能表现或维护状态。
cards.whyItMatters: 若其宣称的广泛适用性得到验证，Scrapling 可能降低开发者在不同抓取规模间切换工具的成本。但目前仅有项目简介，尚无法判断其实际价值。
cards.summary: Scrapling 是 GitHub 趋势项目，自我描述为能处理从单请求到全规模抓取的网络抓取框架。项目作者通过 Discord 和 X 提供支持与技巧。上述信息来自项目简介，实际性能与功能范围需独立验证。
cards.whyItMattersEn: If its claimed broad applicability is validated, Scrapling could reduce the cost for developers switching tools across different scraping scales. However, with only a project description available, its actual value cannot yet be judged.
cards.summaryEn: Scrapling is a GitHub trending project that describes itself as a web scraping framework capable of handling everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl. The author provides support and tips via Discord and X. This information comes from the project's self-description; actual performance and feature scope need independent verification.
cards.title: Scrapling：从单请求到大规模抓取的网络爬虫框架
cards.titleEn: Scrapling: A Web Scraping Framework from Single Requests to Full-Scale Crawls
keyPointsEn: Scrapling positions itself as a web scraping framework covering single requests to large-scale crawls
The project offers daily tips and support through a Discord community and X account
As a GitHub trending project, its actual capabilities should be evaluated based on code and documentation
keyPoints: Scrapling 定位为覆盖从单次请求到大规模抓取的网络抓取框架
项目通过 Discord 社区和 X 账号提供日常技巧与支持
作为 GitHub 趋势项目，其实际能力需结合代码与文档评估
cards.limitationsEn: The input is only a GitHub Trending project description, lacking technical documentation, benchmarks, or user feedback. It is impossible to confirm whether it truly outperforms existing frameworks, nor is its specific feature boundaries, performance, or maintenance status clear.
cards.descriptionEn: Scrapling is a web scraping framework that claims to handle tasks ranging from a single request to full-scale crawling. Its value lies in offering a unified tool for different scraping scales, but actual capabilities require verification against project documentation.

cards.description: 提出一个通过分类、聚合基准风险价格和平衡转移构建保险 tariff 的框架，并基于风险充分性、组合覆盖和反歧视三个准则评估，揭示了多目标权衡的数学关系。
cards.originalTitle: Risk Adequacy and Anti-Discrimination in Insurance Pricing: Classification, Aggregation, and Transfers
cards.limitations: 研究基于理论模型和数值示例，未涉及实际市场数据或监管环境的复杂性；结论的普适性需进一步实证检验。
cards.whyItMatters: 为保险定价中风险基于定价、组合覆盖与反歧视要求之间的权衡提供了形式化分析工具，有助于理解不同政策目标之间的定量关系。
cards.summary: 该研究构建了一个保险定价框架，将定价过程分解为分类、类内基准风险价格聚合和平衡转移三个步骤。作者证明了关于风险充分性、组合覆盖与反歧视准则之间权衡的若干数学结果，包括完美风险充分性的推断阈值、类合并对风险不充分性和推断差异的精确影响等。数值汽车保险研究用于说明这些结果。
cards.whyItMattersEn: Provides a formal analytical tool for understanding trade-offs among risk-based pricing, portfolio coverage, and anti-discrimination requirements in insurance pricing, helping to quantify relationships between different policy objectives.
cards.summaryEn: The study develops an insurance pricing framework that decomposes tariff construction into classification, within-class aggregation of benchmark risk prices, and balanced transfers. The authors prove mathematical results characterizing trade-offs among risk adequacy, portfolio coverage, and anti-discrimination criteria, including an inferential threshold for perfect risk adequacy and exact changes in risk inadequacy and inferential disparity when classes are merged. A numerical motor-insurance study illustrates the results.
cards.title: 保险定价中风险充分性与反歧视的权衡框架
cards.titleEn: A Framework for Risk Adequacy and Anti-Discrimination Trade-offs in Insurance Pricing
keyPointsEn: The framework constructs tariffs through classification, aggregation, and transfers, and evaluates them on risk adequacy, portfolio coverage, and anti-discrimination criteria.
Mathematical results are proven, including an inferential threshold for perfect risk adequacy and exact effects of class merging on risk inadequacy and inferential disparity.
A numerical motor-insurance study illustrates the theoretical findings.
keyPoints: 框架通过分类、聚合和转移构建 tariff，并评估风险充分性、组合覆盖与反歧视三个准则。
证明了完美风险充分性的推断阈值、类合并对风险不充分性和推断差异的精确影响等数学结果。
数值汽车保险研究展示了理论结果的应用。
cards.limitationsEn: The study is based on a theoretical model and numerical examples, without involving real market data or the complexity of regulatory environments; the generalizability of the conclusions requires further empirical testing.
cards.descriptionEn: Introduces a framework for constructing insurance tariffs via classification, aggregation of benchmark risk prices, and balanced transfers, evaluated on risk adequacy, portfolio coverage, and anti-discrimination, revealing mathematical trade-off relationships.

cards.description: 该研究审计FLARE评分流程，发现许多已发布分数由答案抽取规则决定，而非模型表现；这有助于正确解读基准分数并识别规则敏感性。
cards.originalTitle: What FLARE's Published Numbers Actually Measure
cards.limitations: 审计基于已发布分数和特定实验设置，认证规则不变的单元格较少且部分因解析失败；结论是否适用于其他基准或未发布配置需进一步验证。
cards.whyItMatters: 若抽取规则未明确说明，基准分数可能部分反映实现细节而非模型能力，影响模型比较与排行榜解读；作者建议同时报告歧义率、覆盖率和下限。
cards.summary: 作者审计FLARE评分流程，发现部分单元格的分数由答案抽取规则决定，而非模型能力。已发布的34个Headlines分数中，9个与“无输出字节等于Yes”时基准代码返回的四位小数相同，仅4个超过分层多数下限。作者认为未指定抽取规则导致分数部分不可识别，并主张报告分数时需附带歧义率、覆盖率和下限。
cards.whyItMattersEn: If the extraction rule is not specified, benchmark scores may partly reflect implementation details rather than model ability, affecting model comparisons and leaderboard interpretation; the authors recommend reporting ambiguity rate, coverage, and floor together.
cards.summaryEn: The authors audit the FLARE scoring pipeline and find that in some cells the score is determined by the answer-extraction rule, not model ability. Of 34 released Headlines scores, nine equal what the benchmark code returns when no output is byte-equal to Yes at four decimals, and only four clear the per-stratum majority floor. The authors argue that an unspecified extraction rule leaves scores partially unidentified and recommend reporting ambiguity rate, coverage, and floor alongside scores.
cards.title: FLARE评分审计：分数度量的是抽取规则而非模型能力
cards.titleEn: FLARE Score Audit: Scores Measure Extraction Rules, Not Just Model Ability
keyPointsEn: FLARE and lm-evaluation-harness use different extraction rules: the former credits the first entry of the dataset card's choices list found anywhere, the latter takes the first positional match; identical generations differ by up to 0.4216 accuracy.
Of 34 released Headlines scores, nine equal the code's return when no output is byte-equal to Yes, and only four exceed the per-stratum majority floor.
Across a 204-cell factorial and a 46-cell diagnostic, only 10 cells are certified invariant to the rule, four of them only because almost nothing parses.
keyPoints: FLARE与lm-evaluation-harness的抽取规则不同：前者取数据卡选项列表首个出现项，后者取位置首个匹配，同一生成下准确率差异可达0.4216。
已发布34个Headlines分数中，9个等于无输出字节等于Yes时的代码返回结果，仅4个超过分层多数下限。
在204单元格因子实验和46单元格诊断中，仅10个单元格被认证为对规则不变，其中4个因几乎无法解析。
cards.limitationsEn: The audit is based on released scores and specific experimental settings; few cells are certified rule-invariant and some only because parsing fails. Whether conclusions generalize to other benchmarks or unpublished configurations requires further validation.
cards.descriptionEn: The study audits the FLARE scoring pipeline and finds many published scores are driven by answer-extraction rules rather than model performance; this helps interpret benchmark scores correctly and identify rule sensitivity.

cards.description: 该研究首次基于Robinhood Chain三个月全部区块及超5000万笔Uniswap交易，量化了链上需求爆发的形态、构成与扩散特征，区分了事实与模型解释。
cards.originalTitle: Fuji: The Shape, Composition, and Spread of Demand Bursts on Robinhood Chain
cards.limitations: 证据仅来自Robinhood Chain前三个月活跃期，结论外推至其他链或更长期限需谨慎；爆发到达的模型比较仅表明外部触发级联拟合相对更好，并未确立因果；交易者进入后24秒内后续进入增加的原因（模仿或共享信号）未得到识别。
cards.whyItMatters: 该研究将链上拥堵的焦点从gas定价转向需求本身，揭示了爆发期与平静期在交易池、交易笔数和发送者上的结构性差异，为理解区块链市场微观结构提供了新的实证基础。
cards.summary: 研究测量了Robinhood Chain上需求爆发的特征：爆发期交易池数量与平静期相近但重叠少，交易强度更高，峰值中位数为常规负载的2.5倍。需求升降可由小时级慢速与分钟级快速两个指数函数之和描述。作者用外部触发级联与自激两个模型解释爆发到达，前者拟合更优，但未确定交易者进入后的24秒内后续进入增加是模仿还是共享信号所致。
cards.whyItMattersEn: This research shifts the focus of on-chain congestion from gas pricing to demand itself, revealing structural differences between burst and quiet periods in pools, trades, and senders, providing a new empirical basis for understanding blockchain market microstructure.
cards.summaryEn: The study measures demand bursts on Robinhood Chain: bursts trade about as many pools as quiet periods but mostly different ones, with higher intensity, and a median peak 2.5 times the usual load. Both rise and fall of demand are described by the sum of a slow hours-scale and a fast minutes-scale exponential. Two models explain burst arrival—externally triggered cascades fit better than self-excitation—but whether increased entries for about 24 seconds after a trader's entry are due to imitation or a shared signal remains open.
cards.title: Robinhood Chain需求爆发：链上交易突发形态与构成
cards.titleEn: Demand Bursts on Robinhood Chain: Shape, Composition, and Spread
keyPointsEn: Bursts trade 1.05 times the pools of a matched quiet period, but mostly different ones, and trade them harder.
Bursts have 1.40 times the trades and 1.21 times the senders, with a median peak 2.5 times the usual load.
Both demand rise and fall follow a sum of two exponentials with hours-scale and minutes-scale timescales.
keyPoints: 爆发期交易池数量约为匹配平静期的1.05倍，但大部分池不同，且交易强度更高。
爆发期交易笔数为平静期的1.40倍，发送者为1.21倍，峰值中位数为常规负载的2.5倍。
需求上升与下降均呈双指数形态，包含小时级慢过程和分钟级快过程。
cards.limitationsEn: Evidence comes only from Robinhood Chain's first three active months, so extrapolation to other chains or longer horizons requires caution; the model comparison for burst arrival only shows externally triggered cascades fit relatively better and does not establish causality; the cause of increased entries for about 24 seconds after a trader's entry (imitation or shared signal) is not identified.
cards.descriptionEn: This study is the first to quantify the shape, composition, and spread of demand bursts on-chain using every block from Robinhood Chain's first three active months and over 50 million Uniswap swaps, distinguishing facts from model interpretations.

cards.description: 该研究通过两阶段统计检验，区分粗糙Bergomi模型中多尺度行为的来源，发现厚尾收益分布是主因，而非波动率路径的粗糙性或时间记忆。这为金融建模中极端风险估计和期权定价提供了更清晰的机制解释。
cards.originalTitle: Multiscaling in the Rough Bergomi Model: A Tale of Tails
cards.limitations: 研究基于 rBergomi 模型及合成过程（MRW、FLSM）的统计检验，结论限于该模型框架；未涉及真实市场数据的实证，也未评估对其他粗糙波动率模型的推广性。
cards.whyItMatters: 该发现有助于金融建模者更准确识别多尺度性的来源，对极端风险估计、跨期限资产配置及期权定价中尺度假设的选择具有方法学意义。
cards.summary: 论文提出两阶段统计检验程序：先以加权最小二乘回归量化多尺度性，再用保持收益分布但破坏时间相关性的 shuffled surrogates 进行距离置换检验。实证表明，rBergomi 模型的多尺度性主要来自厚尾收益分布，而非记忆效应。作者据此认为，粗糙波动率模型中的表观多尺度性更多是分布属性而非真实时间标度行为。
cards.whyItMattersEn: This finding helps financial modelers more accurately identify the source of multiscaling, with methodological implications for extreme risk estimation, cross-horizon asset allocation, and the choice of scaling assumptions in option pricing.
cards.summaryEn: The paper introduces a two-stage statistical testing procedure: first, weighted least squares regression quantifies multiscaling; second, distance-based permutation tests on shuffled surrogates that preserve return distributions but destroy temporal correlations isolate the source. Evidence shows that multiscaling in the rBergomi model arises primarily from fat-tailed return distributions rather than memory effects. The authors conclude that apparent multiscaling in rough volatility models is largely a distributional property rather than genuine temporal scaling behavior.
cards.title: 粗糙Bergomi模型的多尺度性源于厚尾收益而非记忆
cards.titleEn: Multiscaling in the Rough Bergomi Model Arises from Fat Tails, Not Memory
keyPointsEn: Two-stage test: weighted least squares regression quantifies multiscaling, and distance-based permutation tests separate distributional from memory contributions.
In the rBergomi model, multiscaling primarily stems from fat-tailed return distributions, not temporal correlations.
The procedure is validated for robustness using synthetic processes with known multifractal properties: MRW and FLSM.
keyPoints: 两阶段检验：加权最小二乘回归量化多尺度性，再以距离置换检验区分分布与记忆贡献。
在 rBergomi 模型中，多尺度性主要源于厚尾收益分布，而非时间相关性。
用已知多分形性质的 MRW 和 FLSM 合成过程验证了检验程序的稳健性。
cards.limitationsEn: The study is based on statistical tests of the rBergomi model and synthetic processes (MRW, FLSM); conclusions are confined to this model framework, without empirical evidence from real market data or assessment of generalizability to other rough volatility models.
cards.descriptionEn: This study uses a two-stage statistical testing procedure to disentangle the sources of multiscaling in the rough Bergomi model, finding that fat-tailed return distributions, rather than volatility path roughness or temporal memory, are the primary driver. This offers a clearer mechanistic explanation for extreme risk estimation and option pricing in financial modeling.

cards.description: 该仓库在GitHub趋势日榜中出现，定位为Grok Bot的开源替代方案，并附带可供机器人使用的虚拟机环境。新意在于把代理型机器人与独立虚拟机执行环境打包为开源项目；有用之处是为需要隔离运行环境的机器人开发提供现成参考。
cards.limitations: 输入仅包含项目标题、一句话摘要与来源榜单，未提供代码细节、许可证、依赖项、安全隔离机制、性能数据或维护活跃度。无法判断虚拟机的隔离强度与适用场景，也无法验证其与Grok Bot的替代程度。趋势榜单的出现不等于技术质量或生产可用性的证明。
cards.whyItMatters: 将聊天机器人式代理与虚拟机执行环境结合，是代理类开源工程中值得关注的方向：它为需要在受控环境中运行操作的机器人提供了可参考的开源结构。对于评估自建代理执行环境的开发者，此类项目可作为选型或对比的起点。
cards.summary: 该仓库是托管在GitHub上的开源项目，自述为Grok Bot的替代实现，并为机器人提供可用的虚拟机。事实层面仅能确认其定位与虚拟机这一特性；其内部架构、能力范围与完成度均未在给定信息中说明。作者对项目的具体主张不应视为已验证的结论。
cards.whyItMattersEn: Combining chatbot-style agents with a VM execution environment is a noteworthy direction in open-source agent engineering: it offers a reference structure for bots that need to operate in a controlled environment. For developers evaluating self-hosted agent runtimes, such a project can serve as a starting point for selection or comparison.
cards.summaryEn: This is a GitHub-hosted open-source project describing itself as an alternative implementation of Grok Bot and providing a usable virtual machine for bots. At the factual level, only its positioning and the VM feature can be confirmed; its internal architecture, capability scope and completeness are not described in the given information. The author's specific claims should not be treated as verified conclusions.
cards.title: 开源AI代理机器人获虚拟机运行环境
cards.titleEn: Open-Source AI Agent Bot Gets a Virtual Machine to Run In
keyPointsEn: The project is positioned as an open-source alternative to Grok Bot.
A core feature is a virtual machine environment available to bots.
It appears on a GitHub trending daily list, indicating recent attention.
keyPoints: 项目定位是Grok Bot的开源替代方案。
核心特性是为机器人提供可使用的虚拟机环境。
该项目出现在GitHub趋势日榜，说明近期获得一定关注。
cards.limitationsEn: The input contains only the project title, a one-sentence summary and a trending source; it provides no code details, license, dependencies, security isolation mechanisms, performance data or maintenance activity. The strength of VM isolation and applicable scenarios cannot be judged, nor can the degree to which it substitutes for Grok Bot be verified. Appearance on a trending list is not proof of technical quality or production readiness.
cards.descriptionEn: The repository appears on a GitHub trending daily list, positioned as an open-source alternative to Grok Bot and bundled with a virtual machine that bots can use. Its novelty lies in packaging an agent-style bot with a separate VM execution environment as open source; it is useful as a reference for bot development that needs an isolated runtime.

cards.description: 针对现有因子生成方法探索不足且多智能体易同质化的问题，提出可微对数行列式惩罚直接嵌入联合目标以在训练中保持因子多样性，计算成本随资产数量线性增长，并利用上下文调度器与Shapley交互分析刻画智能体协作结构。
cards.originalTitle: Det-MASO: Diversity-Regularized Multi-Agent Sequential Optimization for Factor Generation
cards.limitations: 证据来自作者在特定基准上的实验报告，1.1%信息系数、6.4%年化收益和0.33夏普比率的提升幅度及统计显著性未在摘要中说明；未提供跨市场、跨资产类别或不同训练窗口的稳健性检验，也未讨论交易成本、换手率与过拟合风险；Shapley交互分析仅刻画合作结构，未证明其与因子样本外表现存在因果关系。
cards.whyItMatters: 为多智能体因子生成中普遍存在的输出同质化问题提供训练期多样性正则化思路，并给出随资产数量线性增长的计算方案，有助于在变化市场中维持因子探索的广度。
cards.summary: 量化投资需要兼具预测性与多样性的alpha因子，现有单智能体方法探索有限，多智能体在共享目标下易输出趋同。作者提出Det-MASO框架，将可微对数行列式惩罚加入联合目标以抑制智能体间相关性，成本随资产数线性增长，并称该惩罚可防止同质均衡。实验报告信息系数提升1.1%、年化收益提升6.4%、夏普比率提升0.33，这些属于作者实验结果陈述而非独立验证结论。
cards.whyItMattersEn: It offers a training-time diversity regularization approach to the common output homogenization problem in multi-agent factor generation, with a computational scheme that scales linearly with the number of assets, helping maintain broad factor exploration in changing markets.
cards.summaryEn: Quantitative investment requires alpha factors that are both predictive and diverse; existing single-agent methods have limited exploration, and multi-agent systems under shared objectives tend to produce similar outputs. The authors propose Det-MASO, which adds a differentiable log-determinant penalty to the joint objective to suppress inter-agent correlation, with cost scaling linearly with the number of assets, and claim the penalty prevents homogeneous equilibria. Experiments report improvements of 1.1% in information coefficient, 6.4% in annualized return, and 0.33 in Sharpe ratio; these are the authors' experimental results rather than independently verified conclusions.
cards.title: Det-MASO多智能体框架优化因子生成多样性
cards.titleEn: Det-MASO Multi-Agent Framework Optimizes Factor Generation Diversity
keyPointsEn: Introduces a differentiable log-determinant penalty into the joint objective to directly penalize inter-agent correlation and preserve factor diversity.
The penalty's computational cost scales linearly with the number of assets, avoiding scalability issues of diversity techniques as the asset universe grows.
Combines a context-conditioned scheduler to dynamically adjust agent emphasis and uses Shapley interaction indices to analyze emergent cooperative structure.
keyPoints: 在联合目标中引入可微对数行列式惩罚，直接惩罚智能体间相关性以保持因子多样性。
惩罚的计算成本随资产数量线性增长，避免多样性技术随资产池扩大而难以扩展。
结合上下文条件调度器动态调整智能体权重，并用Shapley交互指数分析涌现的合作结构。
cards.limitationsEn: Evidence comes from the authors' experimental report on specific benchmarks; the statistical significance and robustness of the reported improvements (1.1% IC, 6.4% annualized return, 0.33 Sharpe ratio) are not detailed in the abstract; no out-of-sample robustness checks across markets, asset classes, or training windows are provided, and transaction costs, turnover, and overfitting risks are not discussed; the Shapley interaction analysis characterizes cooperation structure but does not establish a causal link to out-of-sample factor performance.
cards.descriptionEn: To address limited exploration in existing factor generation methods and homogenization in multi-agent systems, it introduces a differentiable log-determinant penalty directly into the joint objective to preserve factor diversity during training, with computational cost scaling linearly with the number of assets, and uses a context-conditioned scheduler and Shapley interaction analysis to characterize agent cooperation.

cards.description: 该研究建立了条件期望与条件分布关于分层因子的连续性结果，并给出反例界定理论边界；结合神经网络密度结果，得到可容许分层因子的通用逼近定理，为高维连续时间模型中选择有效低维分层因子提供理论依据。
cards.originalTitle: On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing
cards.limitations: 连续性结果与通用逼近定理依赖论文设定的可容许因子类与模型假设，反例表明连续性在一般情形下不成立；数值实验限于两因子高斯短率模型与 Wishart 随机协方差模型，结论的外推需谨慎。
cards.whyItMatters: 为高维连续时间金融模型中神经分层因子的构造提供理论支撑，有助于理解近似误差对条件分布的影响，并为路径依赖产品定价的方差缩减提供可操作依据；但结果基于特定模型设定与数值实验，不构成投资建议。
cards.summary: 论文研究连续时间模型下比例分配蒙特卡洛定价中神经分层因子的构造问题。作者证明相关条件期望与条件分布的连续性结果，并给出反例说明连续性理论的局限；结合神经网络密度结果，得到可容许分层因子的通用逼近定理。数值实验显示学习到的因子在 CMS 区间计息和最差自动赎回产品中优于所考虑的基准。
cards.whyItMattersEn: Provides theoretical support for constructing neural stratification factors in high-dimensional continuous-time financial models, helps understand the impact of approximation error on conditional distributions, and offers an operational basis for variance reduction in pricing path-dependent products; however, results are based on specific model settings and numerical experiments and do not constitute investment advice.
cards.summaryEn: The paper studies the construction of neural stratification factors for derivative pricing under proportional allocation in continuous-time models. The authors establish continuity results for conditional expectations and conditional distributions, provide counterexamples showing the limits of the continuity theory, and combine neural network density results to obtain a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors. Numerical experiments show that learned factors outperform the considered benchmarks in a CMS range accrual and a worst-of autocallable.
cards.title: 神经分层因子用于衍生品定价的连续性理论
cards.titleEn: Continuity Theory for Neural Stratification Factors in Derivative Pricing
keyPointsEn: Establishes continuity results for conditional expectations and conditional distributions with respect to stratification factors, with counterexamples revealing the limits of the continuity theory.
Combines neural network density results to prove a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors.
Numerical experiments in a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model and a Wishart stochastic covariance model show learned factors outperform the considered benchmarks.
keyPoints: 建立条件期望与条件分布关于分层因子的连续性结果，并给出反例揭示连续性理论的边界。
结合神经网络密度结果，证明可容许分层因子的通用逼近定理。
在两因子高斯短率模型与 Wishart 随机协方差模型中的数值实验表明学习因子优于所考虑的基准。
cards.limitationsEn: The continuity results and universal approximation theorem rely on the admissible factor class and model assumptions set in the paper; counterexamples show that continuity fails in general settings. Numerical experiments are limited to a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model and a Wishart stochastic covariance model, so extrapolation of conclusions requires caution.
cards.descriptionEn: The study establishes continuity results for conditional expectations and conditional distributions with respect to stratification factors, provides counterexamples delimiting the theory, and combines neural network density results to obtain a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors, offering a theoretical basis for selecting effective low-dimensional factors in high-dimensional continuous-time models.
